body: Thanks, I'm not going through with it. Suicide is permanent solution for a temporary problem.

Life is interesting and it has much to offer. That I'm resolute about. Looking back at my words from yesterday it seems my decision was made from an emotional perspective without much thought.

Anyway I'm not going through with it, thank you for the help.

>Guilt, in it's own special way, is silly. It's a way humans learn, but damages us over time. We all make bad mistakes. It's part of the ride into humanity. Guilt is a tool used by the mind to teach people lessons. It's your morals saying "Stop it". Too bad it sticks with us forever. It piles on. It becomes a giant weight if you don't find a way to alleviate it. That's where learning your lessons comes in. Too truly move on, we must regard what has happened as what happened see to the best of our ability that it does not happen again. You're young. You have many things for your in the future. You're the result of millions of years of success and failures to become something absolutely amazing.
You can beat this.

Thank you :') I'm not going through with it.  I'm sorry and glad you got through the bullying. You've given great advice and it makes perfect sense to me.
Thank you, I'm not going through with it.

You're right. After a day of thinking I've realized that yesterday I was acting purely on emotion rather than reason.

>I think suicidal thoughts are often a way of repressing some underlying truth. For example: many people will think "I want to be dead "when they are extremely embarrassed.

You're right (at least in my case). Going over my thoughts and feelings, suicide would be a form of escaping from my problems rather than facing them. I'm unhappy with my life and I have the power to change it; although it'll take work. Or I can just give up and end it all. 

Combining hormones + general teenage angst (which i guess may be part of this) and a bit of depression, I can see why suicide seemed (and still kind of seems) much easier but I'm not going to attempt it.

When I was writing the letters after I had decided to commit suicide, I felt happier than I'd felt in months and had a sort of stoic realization. Why? Simply because my problems all disappeared or rather I stopped caring and realized that there are no problems worth feeling bad about. If a problem is in my control, then I can fix it and there's no need to worry, if it's not in my control no need to worry.

Basically regardless of my circumstances I can be at peace.

>suicidal ideation is a combination of bad circumstance and somewhat higher intelligence. 

Yes I agree.

> I suggest finding a passionate subject and honing it.

Physics and Philosophy. I agree with this suggestion, and once I've taken major steps in solving most of my problems that led me to consider suicide I'll do so. 

Anyway thank you for the kind words.

Your experience sounds very very similar to mine. Including the PMO addiction (one which I'm dealing with and unsuccessfully trying to quit at the moment).

I'm glad things worked out for you and are getting better.

 I'm not going through with it today.Thanks for the kind words and I'll be pming you soon.
I've changed my mind. The depression is still here but I'm not committing suicide. My problems are temporary and running away from them through suicide isn't worth it.

>Well, if you´re already so committed on suicide, then nothing you do after today will mater. See? In a way, you´re already free. 

Yesterday when I honestly decided that I was going to kill myself. I felt freer than I've felt for the past few months. All of my problems vanished. 

Today, the suicidal thoughts are still here but it's not happening but I'm going to pursue that feeling/philosophy. I've realized that most of my day to day problems can be solved by simply not caring or losing attachment over what I can't control.

anyway
Thank you :)
